Tiny YOLOv3 object detector

Authors: Joseph Redmon and Ali Farhadi.
The source model is pjreddie's official Tiny YOLOv3 trained on the 80 COCO categories.
  Project and model table: https://pjreddie.com/darknet/yolo/
  Architecture: https://github.com/pjreddie/darknet/blob/master/cfg/yolov3-tiny.cfg
  Weights: https://data.pjreddie.com/files/yolov3-tiny.weights
  Source weights SHA-256: dccea06f59b781ec1234ddf8d1e94b9519a97f4245748a7d4db75d5b7080a42c
  License: LICENSE-Darknet.txt

yolov3-tiny.q8.bin is a local conversion of these weights. Batch normalization is folded into each convolution. Kernels are stored in HWIO order with a signed eight-bit weight and an independent float32 scale for each output channel. The network uses both original detection heads and six anchors on a 416 x 416 letterboxed RGB input. The worker expands the weights to float32 for inference.

The bundled TensorFlow.js Core and WebAssembly backend are version 4.22.0, Copyright Google LLC and contributors, Apache License 2.0. See LICENSE-TensorFlow.txt.
  Project: https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs
  Releases: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tensorflow/tfjs-core/v/4.22.0
            https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm/v/4.22.0

The browser loads the runtime and weights from the same site as this application.

Depth Anything V2 Small

Authors: Lihe Yang, Bingyi Kang, Zilong Huang, Zhen Zhao, Xiaogang Xu, Jiashi Feng and Hengshuang Zhao. The Small model and ONNX conversion are distributed under the Apache License 2.0 (included in LICENSE-TensorFlow.txt).
  Original project: https://github.com/DepthAnything/Depth-Anything-V2
  Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09414
  ONNX export: https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/depth-anything-v2-small/blob/413ce838e669ab7dfc01a6a396bf3d4397286d7f/onnx/model_quantized.onnx
  Converted model SHA-256: fcf51f1b230362b28690bb9d1809bf0431f29cad20534e3f589bd7285547f20d

depth-v2-small.1.bin and depth-v2-small.2.bin are consecutive pieces of the unmodified quantized ONNX export. For inference, the worker assembles the model in memory and processes a resized RGB image with ImageNet normalization. The depth map stores relative inverse depth, scaled per image using the first and 99th percentiles. The model estimates the visible surfaces of one photograph.

refinery-depth.bin is the 518 x 350 prediction on the bundled refinery.jpg (source photo SHA-256 a3f863621247a968cef138142acb81af01ea2817bf5b972be17f3a276d9e9a6e). The first four bytes encode width and height as little-endian uint16 values, followed by row-major 16-bit inverse depth. The starter's train detection also comes from a local Tiny YOLOv3 inference on this source. The application reuses those two fixed outputs on first launch. Newly imported photographs run both models locally, with the depth input capped according to original resolution and available memory.

ONNX Runtime Web 1.22.0 is copyright Microsoft Corporation and contributors, distributed under the MIT License. See LICENSE-ONNX-Runtime.txt and NOTICE-ONNX-Dependencies.txt.
  Runtime: https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/tree/v1.22.0/js/web

Additional license texts for the TensorFlow.js WebAssembly backend are included in LICENSE-XNNPACK.txt, LICENSE-FP16.txt and LICENSE-pthreadpool.txt. The detector can use the bundled TensorFlow.js CPU backend at 288 x 288 on browsers which disable WebAssembly.
